text:
Ava (frontend): heads up — Console heatmap page is loading way slower after last deploy, TTFP jumped for lots of users :eyes:
Luis (platform): saw increased error budget noise too, any deploy id/sha?
Ava (frontend): deploy-bot reported `deploy #2026` around 11:22 UTC (sha: 4f7b2c9). Quick check: main bundle gz size up ~450KB vs previous. FCP for /console/heatmap from telemetry: median 0.8s -> 2.9s in the last 30m.
Maya (prod-obs): confirmed spike in frontend_perf metric starting 1771005100. TTI and FCP both regressed, TTFB steady. Looks like client-side work increased.
Tom (eng-platform): do we have a sourcemap upload for that build? can we profile the built artifact?
Ava (frontend): yes sourcemaps are in S3 under builds/4f7b2c9. I ran `yarn build --profile` locally and saw big chunk from `heatmap-utils.ts` and a new dependency `d3-geo-heat` pulled in by the PR that bumped chart libs.
Sam (design): that PR also added a tile-layer preview on load, maybe rendering a big offscreen canvas?
Luis (platform): if it's a dependency size/regression we should consider a canary rollback via rollout flags for Dedicated customers. For hosted we can apply a fast rollback.
Ava (frontend): quick repro: open console -> navigate to /heatmap, CPU spikes as soon as the page mounts. Devtools profiler shows scripting ~1.7s on main thread. Stackpoints show repeated invocation of `generateHeatTiles` in a sync loop.
Maya (prod-obs): adding profiler snapshot for the 30m window: sampling shows function hot path including `d3-geo-heat.generate` and `renderCanvas` — attaching logs:
```
heatmap: tilesGenerated=524
cpu_main_ms=1723
bundle_main_gzip=1.9MB
module_top=d3-geo-heat
```
Ava (frontend): immediate mitigation options: lazy-load the heatmap module with dynamic import, add virtualization for tile rendering, or revert d3-geo-heat bump. Lazy-load is quick: `const Heatmap = React.lazy(() => import('./Heatmap'));`
Tom (eng-platform): agree lazy-load is low-risk. But also we should push a temporary CDN caching tweak: increase `cache-control` for main.js to allow quicker rollout/rollback without stale clients? careful with immutable fingerprints.
Luis (platform): main.js is fingerprinted, CDN cache is fine. Problem is new code path expensive on mount; caching won't help for CPU. But we can do an immediate canary rollback for hosted route via routing policy: route 100% -> previous version for console.* subdomain while we fix. Will coordinate with infra.
Sam (design): UX impact: heatmap blank placeholder looks bad if we lazy-load; can we show a static SVG placeholder quickly?
Ava (frontend): yep will show low-cost SVG skeleton and then mount heavy canvas after chunk loads. Patch in ~30-60m.
Maya (prod-obs): recommend setting an alert on script_main_scripting_ms > 800ms to auto-notify next time. I can add that.
Tom (eng-platform): next steps: 1) Ava ships lazy-load + placeholder PR (hotfix branch) 2) Maya adds alert & dashboards for heatmap perf 3) Luis toggles canary routing if hotfix not deployable quickly 4) Run `git bisect` if we need to pinpoint commit (but we already suspect chart bump).
Ava (frontend): pushing PR now: https://git.redwood.com/r/redwood/console/pulls/4312 — includes dynamic import and placeholder. Also added a tiny guard: don't generate tiles if viewport < 600px to avoid mobile CPU hit.
deploy-bot: Started deploy of PR 4312 to canary (env=staging) at 11:46 UTC
Luis (platform): staging looks good, CPU drop on staging heatmap from 1.7s -> 0.3s. Nice. If prod rollout looks good we can promote.
Maya (prod-obs): after canary deploy in staging I updated the perf dashboard. New metric med scripting ~320ms. Will monitor for 15m then greenlight
Tom (eng-platform): if we promote, we should do a gradual rollout with feature-flag A/B (10/50/100) for 15m steps to catch regressions on bigger traffic. Also record the rollout in the changelog for postmortem.
Ava (frontend): promoted to 10% in prod via feature flag at 12:05 UTC — monitoring
Maya (prod-obs): 10% looks clean, no errors, perf median ~330ms. Increasing to 50% now.
Sam (design): thanks y'all. Once stable I can tweak placeholder visuals so it doesn't feel janky.
Luis (platform): follow-up items: revert dependency if it doesn't provide clear value; add bundling size budget; add CI check `yarn build --stats` and fail if > X delta; add a runtime guard on heavy operations (setTimeout chunking). I'll open infra tickets.
Ava (frontend): opening ticket for bundle budgets and runtime chunking patterns. Also adding unit tests for memoization on heatmap transforms.
Tom (eng-platform): nice triage. If anyone sees perf rebound after full rollout ping #incidents. Good job catching early. :thumbsup:
Maya (prod-obs): scheduled a mini postmortem doc in confluence, will include timeline + telemetry graphs.
Ava (frontend): thanks all — closing thread once prod is 100% and stable.
deploy-bot: Promote to 50% -> 100% done at 12:28 UTC
